core_obligations: The diagram (proof lines 5695-5709): the commutativity of the diagram of site functors is immediate, the identification of the functor on localized sites with the localization in the induced object follows from the definitions, and the companion result on composition of cocontinuous functors gives the commutativity of the resulting diagram of morphisms of topoi.

The identities (proof lines 5709-5712): the commutativity of that diagram gives the identities for the pullback and the pushforward, and the identity for the lower shriek follows from the adjointness properties of these functors.
proof_roadmap: Check the commutativity of the diagram of site functors and identify the composite with the induced localization.
Use composition of cocontinuous functors to obtain the commutative diagram of topoi.
Read off the three identities, the last by adjointness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that localizing a site twice along a morphism of the site gives a commutative diagram of continuous and cocontinuous functors whose associated diagram of topoi is commutative, with the induced functor identified with the localization in the induced object, and with the expected identities for the lower shriek, the pullback and the pushforward (statement lines 5671-5692). The proof is a short argument: the commutativity of the diagram of site functors is immediate and the identification of the induced functor follows from the definitions (proof lines 5695-5696); the companion result on composition gives the commutative diagram of topoi (proof lines 5697-5709), from which the identities for the pullback and pushforward follow, and the identity for the lower shriek follows from adjointness (proof lines 5710-5712). The non-formal content is the identification of the induced functor. The claim is H1: a short derivation with each input named.
